title: Global concept registry
description: Concepts are global, not per-course. A concept learned in one course is the same concept a later course depends on, so mastery, notes and review carry across, and the crossing is most valuable when the two courses are in different fields. The price is naming discipline: an id must be namespaced, and two entries whose names look alike are flagged for a human to confirm they really are different things.

concept_id.description: Namespaced: <field>.<concept>. The namespace is mandatory precisely because the same word means different things in different fields; without it, sharing concepts across courses silently merges things that are not the same.

aliases.description: Other names the learner or the sources use for this, including other languages.

note_path.description: The single canonical note for this concept. One concept, one note, however many courses touch it.

courses.description: Courses whose curriculum includes this concept.

distinct_from.description: Concept ids that share a name but are NOT the same thing. Recording this once silences the similar-name warning and leaves the decision on the record.
